correctness.rationale: For \(G=K_{n_1,\ldots,n_r}\), a vertex outside \(F\) in part \(V_i\) sees exactly \(|F|-|F\cap V_i|\) members of \(F\), so the fort condition is equivalent to excluding the value one for every non-full selected part. This immediately yields the two minimal two-vertex types and the three-part transversals with at most one singleton selected part. Any larger fort either contains a same-part pair, a pair from two singleton parts, or a three-part transversal of the third type, so no larger fort is minimal. The closed count follows by summing these disjoint types. The inspected verifier independently enumerates every complete multipartite graph type through order nine and checks the literal neighborhood definition against the theorem.

value.rationale: Minimal forts are the hyperedges underlying a standard zero-forcing duality, and complete multipartite graphs are a canonical family. The theorem gives a complete structural classification, a rank-three bound, and an exact count, extending a known bipartite special case. This is a natural exact family result rather than an arbitrary small-instance computation.
residual_risks: Its proof is elementary because complete multipartite adjacency is rigid.
